messages:
maria: quick thought — our continuous-batcher still trips on mixed workloads (short chat + long generation). thinking of a hybrid: slot-based fastpath for tiny requests + tenant microqueues for heavier ones. want to run tradeoffs here.
jonathan: can you sketch the invariant guarantees you want to keep? latency SLO for short requests, fairness for sustained tenants?
maria: exactly. target: p95 <= 50ms for short requests under typical load, and no tenant can starve long-running batches. idea: assign a lightweight slot quota (small token pool) that maps to fastpath microbatches; everything else goes to tenant microqueues that get scheduled by weight.
ashley: sounds similar to lane-based scheduling we've kicked around, but how do you prevent slot hoarding?
maria: two levers: 1) per-slot lease TTL (evict after 10ms if not dispatched), 2) token refill tied to observed request length distribution. refill slow if tenant consistently uses long tokens.
kevin: what's the admission path? sequence: accept -> estimate length -> if est <= small_threshold try fast slot else enqueue to tenant queue? also what about misestimates?
maria: yes. admission pseudocode: ```if estimated_tokens <= FAST_THRESH and free_slot_available: allocate_slot() else enqueue_tenant()``` fallback: if slot was allocated but later turns out long, we preempt the slot and migrate to tenant queue (preempt counter increments).
jonathan: preemption migration costs TLS copy / KV cache rebind — measurable overhead. we should budget preempt rate and add telemetry. also, how do we charge cost across fastpath vs queued?
maria: agree — need explicit telemetry: preempt_count, avg_kv_unpin_time, slot_occupancy_histogram. billing: attribute to original tenant; fastpath simply reduces infra cost, we won't change billing model.
ashley: edge case: burst of tiny requests from noisy neighbor consumes all slots and starves small steady tenant. mitigation: reserve fraction of slots per-tenant or use soft-fair token buckets. any opinions?
kevin: prefer soft buckets with burst credit decay. reserve is safe but reduces utilization. soft approach needs strict eviction rules.
maria: thinking reserve of 10% for tenants with SLA flag, and soft buckets for others. runtime will expose knobs: slot_reserve_pct, preempt_ttl_ms, fast_thresh_tokens. will rollout as feature flag behind canary.
sre-bot: deploy note: when flipping canary, monitor metric `fastpath_preempt_rate` and `p95_short_requests`. alert if preempt_rate > 1% sustained for 5m.
jonathan: rollout checklist: (1) unit tests for preempt migration, (2) integration test with kv-cache warmup, (3) add telemetry dashboards, (4) canary on 5% traffic, (5) abort if p95 regresses >5ms.
maria: thanks — i'll draft RFC follow-up with diagrams + config API. any other concerns?
kevin: add a stress test that simulates misestimation flood (clients sending short then switching to long) — validate eviction hysteresis.
maria: added to the doc TODOs. :thumbsup:
